PART IV CHAMBER FOR MOULD GROWTH TEST

0.

FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part IV ) was adopted

by the Indian Standards Institution on 12 June 1979, after the draft finalized by the Environmental Testing Procedures Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electronics and Telecommunication Division Council. 0.2 The object of this standard ( Part IV) is primarily to guide the environmental equipment manufacturers with respect to broad specifications for their equipment and to assist the users of such equipment to properly define their requirements in the indent of the equipment. The requirements of the equipment largely depend on the conditions of environmental tests to be simulated or created. It is expected that this standard will harmonize the various requirements of the equipment.

0.3 Certain requirements have been specified in a general form in view of ~practical difficulties in defining such requirements quantitatively. It is presumed that with the experience gained, more precise requirements will be laid down for such equipment. 0.4 An overall performance assessment of the complete equipment for a short duration has been included although it may be realized that it may not be entirely sufficient. This will at least ensure the functional performance and operatability of the equipment. Many of the constructional requirements specified can be checked through visual examination. 0.5 In view of the subjective nature of some of the requirements, care shall be taken in using this standard. sufficient

0.6 This standard is one of a series of Indian Standards on equipment for environmental tests for electronic and electrical items. Other standards published so far inthis series are: IS : 9002 Equipment for environmental electrical items: 3 tests for electronic and

IS : 9002 ( Part IV ) - 1979 9002 ( Part I )-I977 Chamber for cold test

9002 ( Part II )-I977 Chamber for dry heat test 9002 ( Part III )-1979 Humidity chamber 9002 ( Part V )-1979 Equipment for vibration ( sinusoidal ) test 9002 ( Part VI )-1980 Constant relative humidity chamber ( noninjection type ) 0.7 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS:2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.
1. SCOPE

( Part IV ) lays down guiding requirements for the design of mould growth chamber required for carrying out mould growth test. 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.1 For the purpose of this standard, the definitions of terms given in IS : 9000 ( Part I )-1977t shall apply. 3. CHAMBER CHARACTERISTICS 3.1 The temperature of the chamber points within the working space. and explanation

1.1 This standard

shall be between 28 and 30�C at all

3.1.1 The temperature of the chamber shall be achieved with a rate of change of temperature not exceeding 1�C per minute averaged over a period of 5 minutes. NOTE - Cooling system may be required in cases where the ambient temperature exceeds28�C. 3.1.2 Any periodic change of temperature per hour. shall not exceed a rate of 1�C

3.2 The relative humidity shall be maintained at a value greater than 90 percent by exposing a large area of water slurry of potassium sulphate. NOTE - In general, for smaller chambers, no aided circulation is recommended. However, larger chamber (2'5 m and above) shall bc fitted with a. suitable fan to provide a gentle circulation of air to all parts of working space to,aid rapid transfer of moisture to or from the salt solution. The speed of circulatmg air shall not be too high otherwise small drops of water or grains of salts on the wall of the tray holding It should also be ensured the s'alt solution may be carried over with the atmosphere. that spores are not detached from item under test by air circulation.

IS : 9002 ( Part IV ) - 1979 3.3 The chamber shall be capable of maintaining the conditions continuously in any single run for at least 84 days. specified

3.4 Unless otherwise specified, the chamber with the instrument console shall be capable of operating at any ambient atmosphere between 0 and 40�C. 4. CONSTRUCTION, 4.1 General 4.1.1 The chamber shall be fabricated preferably with welded steel of sufficient thickness to provide necessary mechanical strength. Corners and seams of the interior liners are to be so welded as to allow for expansion and contraction under all temperature changes to prevent distortion and damage. 4.1.2 The materials used in the interior construction should be proved to be resistant to mould growth. The inside walls shall be of non-corrosive type preferably of stainless steel. 4.2 Working Volume-The working volume of the chamber should be chosen from the following preferred values, unless otherwise specified : O-25, 0'5, 1, 2.5 m3 4.3 Insulation - The chamber shall be suitably and sufficiently insulated. The insulation and insulated space shall be properly sealed so as to prevent exchange of atmosphere between inside and outside. 4.4 Doors - The front door shall be capable of full opening to ensure full access to the working space and fitted with suitable gaskets to prevent exchange of atmosphere between inside and outside. 4.5 Shelves - Removable, perforated shelves capable of supporting without distortion the items of specified mass shall be provided. The number of shelves and adjustable heights are to be wasspecified. The materials used shall be of non-corrosive type. 4.6 Salt Tray - The salt tray or container shall be made of suitable materials which does not craze and which is unaffected by the saturated potassium sulphate solution. The design of the tray shall be such that the tray can be easily cleaned.
NOTE 1 - Attention is drawn to the fact that with the trays of certain materials, salt particles can creep along the walls. NOTE 2 - In order to attain maximum tray shall be as large as possible. rate of moisture transfer, the area of salt

IS : 9002 ( Part IV ) - 1979 6. POWER SUPPLY REQUIREMENTS

6.1 The test equipment shall be capable of operating from an ac supply of

50 Hz either from single phase 240 Vf 10 percent or 3 phase 415 Vf 10 percent. Total power input shall be declared by the manufacturer, if required by the purchaser. 7. SAFETY
7.1 Adequate

electrical safety arrangement shall be incorporated in the chamber design to avoid electric shock to personnel and damage to the chamber. T6e safety protection should be as follows: a) Protection against supply voltage variation; b) Safety cut-outs for temperature beyond 30�C; c) Adequate heat/electrical insulation at control panel; d) Safety alarm ( visual and audio ) in case of chamber functioning, when required; and e) Suitable earth terminal.

9.2 Visual Examination - Each chamber shall be visually examined and inspected for compliance with the relevant requirements of the standard. 9.3 Performance - The chamber shall be subjected to performance run under test conditions stipulated in IS : 9000 ( Part X)-1979* for a minimum period of 28 days continuously.
